Figure 7.1 - logical components, boundary contracts and control assertions for connector management and source sync. 7.1 Connector Contract 7.1.1 Capability discovery Each connector advertises list, fetch, delta cursor, ACL and delete support. Unsupported capabilities trigger a lower-trust ingestion mode and an explicit user-visible warning instead of silent assumptions. At the interface boundary, Connector records shall carry tenant_id, revision, actor_id, occurred_at and a correlation ID wherever the operation changes durable state. The request path POST /v1/connectors/{connectorId}/sync must validate input before allocating a long-running operation; if a dependency is unavailable, callers receive a documented retryable error or a persisted asynchronous job identifier, never an ambiguous success. Engineering verification for this component includes a positive test, a cross-tenant denial test, a duplicate/replay test and an evidence-retention test. The event ConnectorSyncStarted must be visible through correlated logs and the audit record without placing source document text in diagnostic telemetry. 7.1.2 Credential lifecycle OAuth refresh tokens or service credentials live in a dedicated secret store under workspace-scoped references. Operators can revoke credentials, and queued jobs must fail with CONNECTOR_REAUTH_REQUIRED without exposing tokens.

The browser never sends arbitrary tool definitions to the orchestrator. Approval is bound to the reviewed artifact hash, and every cited answer can be traced to immutable source versions. Engineering verification for this component includes a positive test, a cross-tenant denial test, a duplicate/replay test and an evidence-retention test. The event ConnectorSyncStarted must be visible through correlated logs and the audit record without placing source document text in diagnostic telemetry. 7.1.2 Credential lifecycle OAuth refresh tokens or service credentials live in a dedicated secret store under workspace-scoped references.
